issues.body: `_note_graphql_points` raises for a missing or malformed `remaining` value but does not set `_graphql_budget_stop`. `_collect_defuse_prs` catches that refusal per PR and continues its loop, so the next PR issues another `/graphql` request. If GitHub repeatedly returns an errors-only payload, omits `rateLimit`, or returns a malformed meter, every candidate still causes a network request even though none provides evidence that the point bucket remains above reserve. This is fail-open with respect to the resource the new control is intended to preserve: rejecting the response data does not prevent the spend. The `unmeterable` self-test explicitly requires the second request to be issued, so it cannot catch this failure mode.
issues.fix_hint: Latch GraphQL on an unreadable meter (while still refusing the current response), so later `/graphql` calls on that bucket/client are declined before issuance and REST remains unaffected. Change the unmeterable test to perform multiple latch reads and assert one issued GraphQL request, subsequent pre-request refusals, and the corresponding refusal gauge/one-time alert behavior.
issues.title: Unreadable rate meter leaves unbounded GraphQL spending enabled

verdict.summary: The measured-boundary behavior, GraphQL-only latch, REST independence, and unconditional summary gauge are well tested. However, the unreadable-meter path defeats the reserve's core fail-closed purpose: it rejects each returned answer but deliberately leaves the latch open, so every remaining candidate can issue another unmetered GraphQL request. A sustained errors-only or malformed-meter response can therefore consume requests/points through the whole defuse population with no reserve stop. The self-test currently codifies this unsafe behavior rather than testing that subsequent GraphQL spends are prevented.
